checklist.description: The Item Definition contains a clear high‑level functional description and purpose of the system.
System boundaries and all interfaces to other systems and users are explicitly specified.
All intended operating modes (normal, degraded, emergency, etc.) are listed.
Primary and secondary functions of the item, including safety‑related functions, are described.
External actors and their interactions with the item (driver, passengers, other vehicles, infrastructure) are identified.
Relevant operating scenarios (environment, traffic conditions, vehicle state, etc.) are covered.
For each scenario, plausible malfunctioning behaviours (fault conditions) of the item are considered.
At least one potential hazard is identified for every malfunction, describing its impact on vehicle safety.
Severity (S0–S3), Exposure (E0–E4) and Controllability (C0–C3) are estimated for every hazard.
ASIL (or QM) is derived correctly from the S/E/C combination according to the ISO 26262 table.
Safety Goals are formulated for all hazards classified with ASIL ≠ QM.
Each Safety Goal is traceable to its corresponding hazard and states the assigned ASIL.
The rationale for assigning S, E, C and the resulting ASIL is documented.
All Safety Assumptions (SA) and dependencies on other systems/components are listed.
The HARA documentation is complete, consistent and has been reviewed by an independent safety manager.
